clue.text: Brace and bit from builder's toolbox

definitions.meaning: to brace something is to prop it up or support it
a broad-bladed chisel used by bricklayers for cutting bricks

explanation.surface: A handyman reaches for a brace and bit from the builder's toolkit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brace and bit' reads as a single drilling tool, but 'and' splits the clue into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means support or prop up; as a noun it is also a bricklayer's wide chisel.

indicators.note: embracing means the word for yield wraps around the single

parts.note: to budge is to give way or yield
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: Giving way to hug a lone bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A budgie, short for budgerigar, is a small Australian parrot and a common pet bird.

clue.text: People left solitary on ends of railways?

parts.note: one can mean single or solitary, as in 'one man alone'

indicators.note: ends of signals taking the first and last letters of the following word

explanation.surface: People stranded alone at the termini of railway lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People left solitary' reads as one definition, but only 'People' defines; 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Loners are people who prefer to be alone, so they are people of a particular kind.

parts.note: tender is read as legal tender, money, so this describes those who look after funds and pay out money with care

explanation.surface: A tribute to nurses and carers who show tender loving care.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasurers manage and pay out an organisation's money, which is legal tender.

clue.text: Source of Russian river in the country

indicators.note: source of means the opening letter of the next word, as a river starts at its source

parts.note: the Ural is a river flowing through Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: The headwaters of a Russian river lie out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural means relating to the countryside, i.e. located in the country.

indicators.note: inside tells us the word for stuck goes within the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet ground
stuck in the sense of placed or put down, as in 'stuck it on the table'

explanation.surface: Someone accused of having grass hidden away inside, perhaps cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputed and alleged are synonyms: both describe something generally said or believed but unproven.

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, are re-formed into a new order

explanation.surface: Virtuous Conservatives embrace ex-criminals who have changed their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed characters' reads as people who have gone straight; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Righteous means morally upright or virtuous, a synonym of good.

indicators.note: they say signals that the word sounds like another

parts.note: peke is short for Pekingese, a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Someone claiming a particular dog is top dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A peak is the highest point or summit, the top of something.

indicators.note: free suggests the letters are set loose to rearrange

explanation.surface: A remark that free handouts are wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' looks like an adjective meaning splendid; it is slang for a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is slang for a thousand, especially a thousand pounds or dollars.

parts.note: to pass away is to die
rich means wealthy or prosperous

explanation.surface: Spending time with a wealthy film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was a German-American film star, an example of an actress.

indicators.note: before places the abbreviation for died ahead of the stake

parts.note: d is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
an ante is the stake put up before a poker hand

explanation.surface: A gambling author passed away just before placing a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine poet who wrote the Divine Comedy is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Tackle part, keeping mum for performance

parts.note: rig means equipment or gear, as in fishing tackle
ma is an informal word for mother
an actor's role is the part played

explanation.surface: A theatrical description of costume and role, with Mum looking after things.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, tedious procedure, colloquially a 'performance' or palaver.

clue.text: Uncertain rules I tore in pieces

indicators.note: torn in pieces suggests the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone indecisive rips up the regulations they were unsure about.
explanation.definitionFit: Irresolute means hesitant or undecided, a close synonym of uncertain.

clue.text: Addict starts to unload smack, entering rehab

indicators.note: starts to signals taking the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A drug addict should offload their heroin on going into rehabilitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' is slang for heroin, adding to the drug-themed surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for someone who takes drugs habitually, i.e. an addict.

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A novice swimmer in the Serpentine, London's park lake, admits to being inexperienced.
explanation.walkthrough: The Serpentine is a lake in Hyde Park, London, where people swim; here it is the adjective meaning winding.
explanation.definitionFit: Serpentine means winding like a snake, the same as wandering along a twisting course.

clue.text: Contain scare flying across the sea

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters scattering into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Advice to keep calm about fear of flying over the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Transoceanic is an adjective meaning crossing or spanning an ocean.

parts.note: the coy refusal to reveal a secret is read literally as a description of storytelling

explanation.surface: Someone declines to give away a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Narration is the act of telling a story, so it would literally be telling.

clue.text: Shadow of exercise by dead artist

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
a dead limb is numb, without feeling
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A dead painter seen as a shadow of himself after a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: A penumbra is the partially shaded outer part of a shadow.

definitions.meaning: knocking means hitting or hammering, as a clock chimes by hitting
workers who are out are on strike, refusing to work

explanation.surface: Perhaps a boxer flooring an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both hitting something and refusing to work in industrial action.

parts.note: to break in is to enter a building
a jemmy is a burglar's crowbar, used for prising things open

explanation.surface: A bold burglar forces a way in with a crowbar.
explanation.walkthrough: A jemmy is the British word for a short crowbar (US 'jimmy').
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprising means showing bold initiative, close to audacious.

clue.text: Penny left on shelf giving commitment

indicators.note: left on means the penny is placed on top of the shelf, which in a down clue puts it first

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: A coin left on a mantelpiece as a promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a solemn promise or commitment.

clue.text: Consider head of state's surrounded by idiots

indicators.note: surrounded by means the first letter is put inside the idiots

parts.note: asses are fools or idiots

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A head of state reflects on being surrounded by fools.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to evaluate or consider something carefully.

parts.note: U is an old British label for upper-class usage
nit is British slang for a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: A rude remark that a division's upper-crust member is an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper-class comes from the 1950s 'U and non-U' debate on British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single component or section of a larger whole.

clue.text: Trifles with femmes fatales, holding a gun

indicators.note: holding means the beauties contain the other pieces

parts.note: belles are beautiful women, loosely femmes fatales
gat is old American slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: A dismissive aside about seductive women brandishing a pistol in a film noir.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelles are things of little importance, synonymous with trifles.

parts.note: c is the abbreviation for cloudy in weather notation
to rid is to free of something

explanation.surface: A cloudy beer given away free, a pint of bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter here is not the British beer but an adjective for a sharp taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid means sharp and bitter in taste or smell.

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A diner says a sauce goes well with everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' reads as a condiment; it is cheek or impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce in the sense of cheek or impudence is a synonym of the brazen nerve called gall.

clue.text: Officer rose perhaps, accepting one grand promotion

indicators.note: accepting means the bush takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: brier is a thorny bush such as the wild rose, so rose is an example
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
ad is short for advertisement, a promotion
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An army officer named Rose, perhaps, gets a big step up in rank.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose looks like a person's name; it is the flower, and brier is a wild rose.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is a senior army officer ranking above colonel.

clue.text: Non-mainstream single, opening of 'Not Fade Away'

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single

indicators.note: opening of signals taking the first letter of the next word

parts.note: to die away is to fade away, so die means fade

explanation.surface: A review of an alternative record released as a single, Not Fade Away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not Fade Away' looks like a song title to keep whole; it splits into the first letter of Not and a verb for fade away.
explanation.definitionFit: Indie describes independent music or film outside the commercial mainstream.

indicators.note: from signals the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone arriving at Lubango airport has just touched down.
explanation.walkthrough: Lubango is a city in Angola, so the hiding place doubles as the person's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the southern African country whose capital is Luanda is a person of that nationality.

indicators.note: in places the turned soldier inside the outfit

parts.note: a dress is an outfit or set of clothes

indicators.note: back means the word for soldier is read in reverse

parts.note: GI is the usual term for an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier wanders off again in his uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stray' looks like a stray soldier; it is the definition, a verb for wandering off topic.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to stray from the main subject when speaking or writing.
